title: SignalError
description: Something in the pipeline broke, said in a way another system can route rather than only print. The only event not about one piece of content: it is about a step that failed and who answers for it. Keys are snake_case, not the camelCase the rest of leaf uses: this travels inside a Liquid envelope, whose own fields (event_id, occurred_at, event_type, owner_unit_ref) are snake_case and pinned byte-exact by signed golden vectors. The shape follows the wire.

signal_id.description: The signal's own id, written where it was raised, so the same failure reported twice can be recognised as one.

code.description: A machine-readable code such as ENRICHMENT_TIMEOUT. Free text: the vocabulary belongs to whoever raised it, and a reader matches on it rather than on the summary.

summary.description: What went wrong, for a person. Never the whole trace.

source.description: The module that raised it, such as creativeflow.worker.process_asset. Says where to look, not who is at fault.

owner_unit_ref.description: The session or unit the failure belongs to. Who answers for it, which is how an error finds somebody at all.

severity.description: How bad it is, as judged where it was raised.

status.description: Where the handling of it stands. Raised as reported; moved on by whoever picks it up, not by whoever raised it.

occurred_at.description: When the failure happened. Carried inside the payload as well as on the event, because the signal outlives the event that delivered it.

correlation_id.description: The trace this failure belongs to, for tying it to others from the same run.

subject_ref.description: The thing that was being worked on when it broke, when there is one.

metadata.description: Whatever else the raising step knew — the asset, the stage it stopped at. Keys belong to that step, so none are fixed here.
